summary: Feed s125_double is degraded: 8.4% duplicate packets and 97.2% encrypted bytes exceed NDR tolerances, reducing detection coverage and wasting analysis capacity.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is aggregating overlapping SPAN/TAP sources (likely same traffic from two switch SPANs or dual TAPs) without deduplication, so the same packet arrives twice within milliseconds.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR wastes CPU/storage on duplicate flows, inflates connection counts and alerts, and can skew behavioral analytics and deduplication-dependent detection.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication (e.g., 5-10ms window, hash on IP ID/TCP seq) to suppress the 8.4% duplicates before the 10G NDR port while preserving both directions and full payload the NDR needs.

findings.root_cause: 97% of bytes are TLS/encrypted, above the NDR's 90% tolerance. Traffic is not being decrypted or selective cleartext is not being forwarded, so payload is opaque.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires full payload for detection; with 97% encrypted it is effectively blind, cannot do IDS signatures, JA3, or payload analytics, severely reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Deploy or tune SSL visibility/decryption upstream of the packet broker and forward decrypted copy to NDR per policy, or feed NDR with decrypted traffic from proxy/visibility appliance to restore payload inspection without breaking privacy/compliance.
